optimized_sql:
WITH sales_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_dim WHERE d_moy = 4 AND d_year = 1999
),
returns_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_dim WHERE d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10 AND d_year = 1999
),
catalog_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk FROM date_dim WHERE d_moy BETWEEN 4 AND 10 AND d_year = 1999
),
store_bridge AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT ss.ss_store_sk, ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_customer_sk,
           MAX(ss.ss_net_profit) AS ss_net_profit,
           MAX(sr.sr_net_loss) AS sr_net_loss
    FROM store_returns AS sr
    JOIN store_sales AS ss
      ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
     AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
     AND ss.ss_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM sales_dates)
    WHERE sr.sr_returned_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM returns_dates)
    GROUP BY ss.ss_store_sk, ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_customer_sk
),
catalog_agg AS (
    SELECT cs.cs_bill_customer_sk, cs.cs_item_sk,
           MAX(cs.cs_net_profit) AS cs_net_profit
    FROM catalog_sales AS cs
    JOIN (
        SELECT DISTINCT b.ss_customer_sk, b.ss_item_sk
        FROM store_bridge AS b
    ) AS pairs
      ON pairs.ss_customer_sk = cs.cs_bill_customer_sk
     AND pairs.ss_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_sold_date_sk IN (SELECT d_date_sk FROM catalog_dates)
    GROUP BY cs.cs_bill_customer_sk, cs.cs_item_sk
),
fact_agg AS (
    SELECT b.ss_store_sk, b.ss_item_sk,
           MAX(b.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
           MAX(b.sr_net_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
           MAX(ca.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
    FROM store_bridge AS b
    JOIN catalog_agg AS ca
      ON ca.cs_bill_customer_sk = b.ss_customer_sk
     AND ca.cs_item_sk = b.ss_item_sk
    GROUP BY b.ss_store_sk, b.ss_item_sk
)
SELECT i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name,
       MAX(f.store_sales_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       MAX(f.store_returns_loss) AS store_returns_loss,
       MAX(f.catalog_sales_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM fact_agg AS f
JOIN item AS i ON i.i_item_sk = f.ss_item_sk
JOIN store AS s ON s.s_store_sk = f.ss_store_sk
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. Predicate pushdown via date_sk lookup — TARGET: date_dim d1/d2/d3 joins and the filters on ss_sold_date_sk, sr_returned_date_sk, cs_sold_date_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Replace the three date-dimension joins with direct date_sk range/list filters on each fact table so April-1999 sales, Apr–Oct-1999 returns, and Apr–Oct-1999 catalog sales are isolated before any multi-table join.

2. Build and pre-aggregate the store-side bridge — TARGET: store_sales ⋈ store_returns on ss_ticket_number=sr_ticket_number, ss_item_sk=sr_item_sk, ss_customer_sk=sr_customer_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Start from the date-filtered store_returns rows, probe store_sales by its primary key, and collapse the result to one row per (ss_store_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_customer_sk) with MAX(ss_net_profit) and MAX(sr_net_loss); the final MAX over store/item is preserved because it is a max over per-customer maxima.

3. Pre-aggregate catalog_sales to one row per customer/item, restricted to bridge pairs — TARGET: catalog_sales row-level join on cs_bill_customer_sk=sr_customer_sk AND cs_item_sk=sr_item_sk — TRANSFORMATION: First take the distinct (ss_customer_sk, ss_item_sk) pairs from the store-side bridge, then compute MAX(cs_net_profit) per (cs_bill_customer_sk, cs_item_sk) over only the d3-filtered catalog_sales rows matching those pairs; join this compact aggregate back to the bridge, eliminating the multiplicative fan-out of multiple catalog orders per return.

4. Defer small dimension joins — TARGET: store and item joins in the large fact join — TRANSFORMATION: Carry only s_store_sk and i_item_sk through the fact aggregations, then join store and item after the final grouping to obtain s_store_id/s_store_name/i_item_id/i_item_desc, keeping the expensive join narrow and avoiding row-width blowup.

5. Materialize the reusable bridge — TARGET: the store-side (ss_store_sk, ss_item_sk, ss_customer_sk) aggregate — TRANSFORMATION: Compute this bridge once in a materialized CTE/derived relation and reuse it both for the catalog pre-aggregation semi-join and for the final join/group, so the expensive store_sales×store_returns work is not evaluated twice.
